parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional household/customer survey with exploratory comparative analysis across provinces
parsed.population_and_sample: Water-service customers in sampled neighbourhoods across nine Iraqi provinces/sites; 2,356 completed questionnaires, generally using random samples from customer lists and quasi-random household sampling in Karbala.
parsed.exposure: State/utility water-service delivery performance, particularly continuity and the perceived fairness or equity of service provision; contextual comparison with electricity-service performance.
parsed.outcome: Satisfaction with water-service continuity and willingness to pay for service improvements, the latter used as a proxy for trust in the state; findings also address service availability and unequal provision.
parsed.rationale: The “Water services survey” section (pp. 282–283) reports primary survey data on water use, continuity, quality, pressure, priorities, and willingness to pay, with the sampled populations and procedures identified in Table 1. The “Findings” section (pp. 283–288) empirically examines how state/utility service performance and equitable distribution relate to satisfaction, willingness to pay, trust, and legitimacy, providing access-relevant outcomes and a governance mechanism.
